title: Quantex Review 2026: Sign Up or Stay Away?
description: Quantex review: what its site claims about a $250 deposit, AI trading and a 4.6/5 rating, and what to check before you sign up.
author: James Whitmore
excerpt: Quantex promotes AI trading with a $250 minimum and a 4.6/5 rating, but names no operator or regulator.
content:
Quantex is presented as an AI-assisted trading platform with automated trades, a demo account and a $250 starting point. There is no operator, regulator or licence number on the page, and the only performance measure is a 4.6/5 rating that has no named source.

The summary table lists bank cards only, while the body adds PayPal and Skrill. The asset table lists shares, but the body lists crypto. We explain the page's own claims here and flag each point we were unable to check.

Quantex at a Glance

Here is what the platform's own page states and what it leaves out.

CategoryWhat the page says
Platform typeAI-assisted trading with automatic and manual modes
Minimum deposit$250, currency not named
FeesNone stated. No schedule given
Payment methodsCards, PayPal, Skrill and bank transfer, with other options unnamed
WithdrawalsUsually within 24 hours. No limits given
SupportDescribed as 24/7, with no channels listed
Regulator or licenceNot stated
OperatorNot named

Items come from the platform's own page. We have not tested the platform.

Is Quantex Legit? What the Claims Show

Automatic execution and signal claims

The page says AI and machine learning generate signals and can place trades automatically, with a manual mode for users who prefer control. Without the strategy, model or risk limits set out, the page offers no way to test what it says.

Performance and ratings

The page refers to a high success rate and notable gains from a small deposit, but gives no return figures, time period, sample size or method. Neither a source nor a review total accompanies the 4.6/5 rating.

Asset coverage

The summary table lists bank cards only, while the body adds PayPal and Skrill. The asset table lists shares, but the body lists crypto. Ahead of registration, the page gives no clear picture of the markets that are actually open to you.

Costs and Minimum Deposit

The page states a $250 minimum deposit and says there are no registration, transaction or withdrawal fees. Fee schedules, spreads and payment-provider charges are all missing.

This review uses a 250 baseline in your own currency, so that is AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK and EUR 250 in European Union countries. Because the currency for the $250 figure is not stated, look up the exact amount and its currency in the terms first.

Who Is Behind Quantex

The page names no legal entity, company number or address. The sign-up links lead to coinpulse.cc, a third-party domain, and nothing on the page says whether the publisher is paid through them.

Is Quantex a Scam? Withdrawals and Complaints

Searches for Quantex often ask whether it is a scam, whether withdrawals work and whether there are complaints. According to the page, withdrawals are typically processed within a day, yet no limits, timelines or complaints process are given.

Find independent complaint records and reviews with named sources before you put any money in. Neither a rating nor a set of favourable testimonials shows how withdrawals are processed.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Find the legal company behind Quantex and check it against your national regulator's register.
  • Before depositing, obtain a written list of all fees, including the spreads and withdrawal costs.
  • Seek out performance history that you can check and that carries dates, not just a single score.
  • Start small, using only what you can afford to lose, and practise on the demo first.

Risk factors to weigh before you join

The main risk is an unnamed operator, because a user has no clear party to hold to account. The page's conflicting claims increase the risk. A system that places trades for you does not remove the risk that those trades lose money.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Quantex legit?

The site makes claims about Quantex but names no operator, regulator or licence number. The company registry and the regulator's register should both be consulted before any deposit.

What is the minimum deposit for Quantex?

The currency behind the $250 figure is not specified on the page. Confirm both the sum and the currency in the terms before paying anything.

Is Quantex regulated?

The page does not identify a regulator or licence, and the brokers it mentions go unnamed. Your national regulator's register is where to look for the company running the service.

Does Quantex charge fees?

No fees are claimed, yet the page sets out no schedule for spreads, withdrawals or currency conversion. Read the full terms first.

Does the use of automation eliminate the chance of loss?

No. A system that places trades for you does not remove the risk that those trades lose money.

Our Verdict on Quantex

Quantex's page makes broad claims without naming an operator, a regulator or verifiable results. Our rating reflects these gaps. Once the operator and its claims are confirmed, we will revisit this review. Risk nothing you cannot afford to write off.
